Its API posture is that of a regulator: two real programmatic surfaces, both attached to a statutory register rather than to a platform. The ACMA Spectrum Licensing API is fully public and anonymous — a WCF service at api.acma.gov.au exposing 22 REST operations (XML and JSON projections of eleven web methods) plus a SOAP endpoint and a live WSDL, letting anyone query licences, licensees, transmitter sites, device registrations, antennas, access areas and the 400 MHz band register, capped at 2,000 records per query. The Do Not Call Register's Real Time Access washing service is a live, publicly-retrievable ColdFusion SOAP WSDL whose three operations require a paid industry subscription, alongside an SFTP automated washing channel at sftp.donotcall.gov.au. ACMA also runs an Azure API Management developer portal at developer.acma.gov.au that is entirely behind a sign-in wall. Public register and licence bulk data is published as daily file downloads and on data.gov.au rather than as a queryable API. ACMA is a regulator, not an operator, so it sits outside the CAMARA and GSMA Open Gateway commitment layer entirely; no CAMARA reference was found anywhere in its public surface.

companies.name: Beatport
companies.description: Beatport is the leading online music store and streaming platform for electronic dance music DJs and producers, founded in 2004 and headquartered in Denver, Colorado. Beatport sells high-quality downloads (lossless WAV, AIFF, and FLAC, plus AAC) of tracks, releases, and DJ tools across more than 150 electronic genres, and operates a subscription streaming tier — Beatport Streaming — that delivers catalog tracks directly into supported DJ applications and hardware including Pioneer DJ rekordbox, Serato DJ Pro, Denon DJ Engine DJ, Algoriddim djay, Virtual DJ, Traktor, and others through integration partners. The Beatport Group also operates Beatsource (open- format DJ streaming and download store), DJCity (open-format record pool), Beatport LINK and Beatsource LINK (in-app streaming for DJ software), BeatportAmp (distribution and rights management for labels, formerly Ampsuite), Plugin Boutique (audio software and plugin marketplace), Loopcloud (sample subscription for producers), Label Radar (demo submission), Beatport Live (live events and streaming), Beatportal (editorial and media), and the International Music Summit (IMS) industry conference. The company reports ten million registered users, eighty thousand labels, four hundred thousand artists, and four hundred million USD paid out to rights holders since launch. Beatport operates a v4 REST API at api.beatport.com governed by OAuth 2.0 (authorization-code grant) with an interactive Swagger-UI developer portal at /v4/docs/; access is gated to approved partners through the Beatport Partner Portal, and there is no public client-credentials tier for general developers. The API exposes the Beatport catalog (tracks, releases, artists, labels, genres, sub-genres, charts, playlists, my-beatport collections, holds, and DJ-oriented search filters such as BPM, key, and released-date) and is the same surface that powers the public beatport.com applications and third-party DJ-software integrations. Beatport does not publish a downloadable OpenAPI document, an official SDK, or a CLI; partner integration is brokered case-by-case through the Partner Portal and the business-development team.

Firstory layers on second-by-second analytics, dynamic ad insertion, membership subscriptions, listener donations, cross-promotion, a personal website builder, the Flink universal link, and embeddable players. Theta operates as Theta Labs, headquartered in San Jose, California.

companies.name: Klout
companies.description: Klout was a San Francisco social-analytics company, founded in 2008 by Joe Fernandez and Binh Tran, that scored individuals on their online social influence. The "Klout Score" was a single number from 1 to 100 derived from the size of a person's social network and how other people engaged with the content they published across connected accounts such as Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, and Google+. Klout operated a public REST API — the Klout API v2 at api.klout.com — that let developers resolve a social handle to a Klout identity, look up a user's score and score history, and retrieve influence graphs (who a user influences and is influenced by) and topic affinities; access was key-based and widely used by marketing, CRM, and social-listening tools, and a large community of third-party client libraries grew up around it in Ruby, Node.js, Python, and PHP. Lithium Technologies acquired Klout on 27 March 2014 for approximately $200 million. Lithium retired Klout as a standalone service on 25 May 2018 — the day the EU General Data Protection Regulation took effect — stating that Klout's AI and machine-learning capabilities were valuable to Lithium but the consumer service was not aligned with its long-term strategy. The Klout API was shut down with the service. Lithium has since been rebranded as Khoros, and klout.com now redirects into the Khoros website. The company is defunct and operates no live API; this profile is retained as a historical provider record in the API Evangelist network.

As a generalist, Slow invests across consumer and social, fintech, SaaS and enterprise/developer tools, healthcare, crypto/web3, the creator economy, and real-world operations (SMB acceleration, buyouts/rollups, franchising). The firm runs a dedicated Creator Fund backing creator-led businesses, and has deployed roughly $800M+ across multiple fund vintages since inception. Notable investments include Pinterest, Slack, Robinhood, Nextdoor, Postmates, Opendoor, Wealthfront, Casper, PillPack, Airtable, Gusto, and Solana.

companies.name: Social Capital
companies.description: Social Capital is a technology investment firm founded in 2011 by Chamath Palihapitiya (a former Facebook executive) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with co-founders Mamoon Hamid and Ted Maidenberg. Originally a traditional venture fund that stood out by backing healthcare, financial services, education, and other hard, regulated sectors the VC community had neglected, the firm pivoted in 2018 into a technology holding company that stopped accepting outside capital and now invests from its own permanent balance sheet of roughly $2.1B, aiming to "earn like Berkshire Hathaway and invest like the Red Cross." Its thesis targets multiple emerging $10T markets across deep tech commercialization, life sciences and drug discovery, the global energy transition, and creator-economy media. Chamath became known as the "SPAC King" for taking companies public through the Social Capital Hedosophia (IPOA-IPOF) vehicles, including Virgin Galactic, Opendoor, Clover Health, and SoFi. Notable investments include Slack, Box, SurveyMonkey, Wealthfront, Netskope, Intercom, Groq, Palmetto, Saildrone, and Relativity Space.

companies.description: Visioconference (video conferencing) is a category of communication technology enabling real-time visual and audio communication between remote participants. This repository profiles the video conferencing API ecosystem including leading providers such as Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Webex, Digital Samba, VideoSDK, Daily.co, and others offering REST APIs for embedding and managing video conferencing functionality.
